findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare `pass` body, dropping its previous concrete `evaluate` implementation. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`) that are not implemented here, so the class is abstract. `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, which will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for any `Detector` whose `type` is `metric_alert_fire`, instead of returning a handler or `None`. `process_detectors` does not catch this, so a single metric-alert detector in the list would crash processing for the whole data packet. Either implement the abstract methods or keep a concrete stub implementation. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector` comment above the class is also now stale.

findings.title: Expected occurrence built with wrong group key in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` the expected occurrence is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` while `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with group key `"group_key"`. The handler's real `build_occurrence_and_event_data` call will produce a fingerprint of `[f"{detector.id}:group_key"]`, whereas the expected one has `[f"{detector.id}:val1"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass whose equality includes `fingerprint`, so either this assertion fails, or (if it passes) the comparison is not actually verifying the fingerprint, meaning the new occurrence hook is not meaningfully tested for correct group-key-based fingerprinting. Use `"group_key"` when building the expected occurrence.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still states "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". The docstring should be updated to describe the dict keyed by group key so implementers of the abstract `DetectorHandler.evaluate` are not misled about the contract.
